column2: Security Awareness Training should assist employees to:\nunderstand the need for policies, procedures, and technical controls, along with their justification, implementation, and enforcement. within the organization.become aware of individuals, either inside or outside the organization, who might try to co-opt them into activities counter to the organization’s mission.detect and report disruptive behavior by employees.monitor adherence to organizational policies and controls.monitor and control changes to organizational systems (e.g., to prevent the installation of malicious code) .require separation of duties between employees who modify data and those who approve modifications.detect and report violations of the security of the organization’s facilities and physical assets.plan for potential incident response proactively

Social Engineering Training could be part of an organization’s security awareness training program. However, due to social media uprising trend, dedicated training program could assist in:\nestablishing, monitoring, and enforcing proper and legit social media policies.understanding data classification levels.understanding data classification levels.understanding data classification levels.outlining ways in which information exposed in social media may be used (including for potential recruitment into a crime organization or extremist groups).comprehending what type of data can be collected from a randomly selected profile

Training on reducing risks to customer service processes should focus on:\nprotecting computer accounts used in these processes.auditing access to customer records.auditing access to customer records.auditing access to customer records .auditing access to customer records.ensuring consistent enforcement of defined security policies and controls.implementing proper system administration safeguards for critical servers.implementing proper system administration safeguards for critical servers.using secure backup and recovery methods to ensure availability of customer service data

Refresher Training needs to cover all facets of an organization, not just information security. Training should encompass the following topics:\nhuman resources.legal counsel.legal counsel.legal counsel.physical security, and.any others of interest.Training can include, but should not be limited to:\nchanges to policies. issues that have emerged over the past year. information security trends

Management Training should assist participants to:\nrecognize and respond to inappropriate or concerning behavior in employees.consistently investigate and respond to all rule violations.monitor indications by employees of possible financial problems or unexplained financial gain.

Human Resources Training should focus on:\nthe insider threat policies and the processes that address them across the organization.the insider threat policies and the processes that address them across the organization.the foundation, maintenance, and constant enhancement of an employee assistance program (EAP)

Legal Counsel Training should focus on:\nreviewing insider threat policies .analyzing issues that arose in the past year . analyzing issues that arose in the past year. outlining strategies to avoid similar incidents in the future

Physical Security Training should focus on:\nreviewing policies and procedures for access to company facilities by employees, contractors, and trusted business partners.reviewing any policies on prohibited devices (USB devices, cameras, etc.).proper handling of the organization’s physical assets as well as evacuation or emergency procedures that may arise in the event of an emergency

Data Owners Training should focus on:\ndiscussing projects that may have heightened risk of insider threat, for example, strategic research projects that will involve creation of new trade secrets.identifying the value of an organization’s IP (Intellectual Property) and the potential damage associated with an insider attack.

Information Technology Training should focus on:\nefficiently educating employees on procedures for recognizing viruses and other malicious code.identifying which devices should be prohibited or permitted for authorized use on the various information systems within the organization
Software Engineering Training should focus on effective auditing of configuration management logs to detect insertion of malicious code.
